definition: Highest METR 80%-success time horizon (human task length, minutes) among models RELEASED by the end of the obs period (model dating, as in the *-by-release ids), per METR-Horizon-v1 benchmark_results.yaml (the pilot-2025 file vintage, Wayback 2026-01-12); kept as the pilot-2025 history, the *-by-release ids carry the current vintage

Highest METR 50%-success time horizon (human task length, minutes) among models RELEASED by the end of the obs period (model dating, as in the *-by-release ids), per METR-Horizon-v1 benchmark_results.yaml (the pilot-2025 file vintage, Wayback 2026-01-12); kept as the pilot-2025 history, the *-by-release ids carry the current vintage

Release-cohort METR 80%-success time horizon (human task length, minutes): the highest point estimate among models RELEASED on or before the obs date (model release_date), per the METR evaluation vintage retrieved (benchmark_results_1_1.yaml; later METR re-estimates are appended as revisions). Not the frontier as publicly evaluated at that date: METR evaluations appear after release

Release-cohort METR 50%-success time horizon (human task length, minutes): the highest point estimate among models RELEASED on or before the obs date (model release_date), per the METR evaluation vintage retrieved (benchmark_results_1_1.yaml; later METR re-estimates are appended as revisions). Not the frontier as publicly evaluated at that date: METR evaluations appear after release

Release-cohort Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI; Epoch AI's item-response fit over many benchmarks, unbounded scale anchored at Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130 and GPT-5 = 150): the highest ECI point estimate among models RELEASED on or before the obs date (the model's release date, Epoch's `date`), per the current vintage of epoch_capabilities_index/eci_scores.csv in Epoch AI benchmark_data.zip (CC-BY 4.0); series from 2023-03-14 (GPT-4); earlier dates re-stated when Epoch refits

Release-cohort Remote Labor Index automation rate (Scale AI + Center for AI Safety; share of 240 real Upwork freelance projects whose AI deliverable expert graders judge at least as good as the professional one, %): the highest score among models RELEASED on or before the obs date, per Epoch AI's mirror rli_external.csv in Epoch AI benchmark_data.zip (CC-BY 4.0) (Scale's leaderboard has no data file or release dates)

METR-equivalent software task horizon at 50% success (human expert hours): eci-frontier-by-release converted by the frozen calibration log2(METR p50 minutes) = -26.366541 + 0.226507 * ECI (OLS over the 21 models in both METR's Time Horizon 1.1 file and the ECI file of 2026-10-15; 4.415 ECI points per doubling, R^2 0.971, residual sd 0.46 doublings), divided by 60; obs = the ECI frontier dates, and any date already in the ledger re-stated as of that date (gather/collectors/robots_software.py)

Remote-freelance-work task horizon at 50% success (human hours): the horizon h at which METR's logistic success model (slope 0.6 per doubling of task length, METR's overall-score method of 2025-07-14), averaged over RLI's projects, equals rli-automation-by-release / 100; the projects are the 201 of 240 with a completion time, reconstructed from the RLI paper's Fig. 4 histogram (12 log bins, projects spread evenly in log time within a bin) plus its stated min 0.2 h and max 450 h; no value at 0% or 100%; obs = the RLI frontier dates, and any date already in the ledger re-stated as of that date (gather/collectors/robots_software.py)

Blended AI task horizon at 50% success (human hours): the geometric mean sqrt(software x remote) of horizon-50-software-eci and horizon-50-remote-rli in force on the obs date (computed from the unrounded components), one row per date on which either component changed, from the first date both exist (2025-06), plus any date already in the ledger re-stated as of that date

METR-equivalent software task horizon at 80% success (human expert hours): eci-frontier-by-release converted by the frozen calibration log2(METR p80 minutes) = -28.242299 + 0.222614 * ECI (OLS over the 21 models in both METR's Time Horizon 1.1 file and the ECI file of 2026-10-15; 4.492 ECI points per doubling, R^2 0.966, residual sd 0.49 doublings), divided by 60; obs = the ECI frontier dates, and any date already in the ledger re-stated as of that date (gather/collectors/robots_software.py)

Remote-freelance-work task horizon at 80% success (human hours): horizon-50-remote-rli (unrounded) divided by 2^(ln 4 / 0.6) = 4.96, the task length at which the same logistic model (slope 0.6 per doubling) predicts 80% success; no value at 0% or 100%; obs = the RLI frontier dates, and any date already in the ledger re-stated as of that date (gather/collectors/robots_software.py)

Blended AI task horizon at 80% success (human hours), the robots-software KPI: the geometric mean sqrt(software x remote) of horizon-80-software-eci and horizon-80-remote-rli in force on the obs date (computed from the unrounded components), one row per date on which either component changed, from the first date both exist (2025-06), plus any date already in the ledger re-stated as of that date

Precursor of the-linux-kernel-patch, the human-submitted side (AI-written code that a person submits): the largest single code contribution (patch, patch series or pull request) substantially written by AI (the contributor, the project or its maintainers state that an AI system wrote most of the code; a human may have designed it, but work whose author claims most of the writing, or says only that AI helped, does not count, e.g. Node.js node:vfs, 2026-05-23: 'created by me with massive help from @claude. The design of this feature is mostly mine') that was merged into a major open-source project (OS kernel, compiler, language runtime, browser engine, core library, or a comparably maintained project), in lines added per the merge record; obs = merge date; a row only when the record grows. Independent acceptance only (owner 2026-10-28): maintainers other than the submitter approved it, in a project that neither the submitter nor the AI system's developer controls (owns it, or leads it alone); so not a project lead merging their own contribution (Ladybird's Andreas Kling, 2026-02-24), nor a project owned by the AI developer (Bun, Anthropic, 2026-05-14). The note names the project and the AI system, who submitted it and who approved it

Precursor of the-nature-author: the highest venue tier at which a paper substantially generated by AI (by the authors' account the AI posed or chose the question, ran the work and wrote the paper; humans at most selected, formatted or submitted) was accepted after human peer review: 1 = workshop of a major conference, 2 = main track of a major conference or a peer-reviewed journal outside the top tier, 3 = top field journal, 4 = Nature or Science; venues reviewed only by AI do not count; obs = acceptance (announcement) date; a row only when the tier rises; a later withdrawal is noted, the rung still counts

Precursor of the-10m-solopreneur, the human side (solo founders handing ever more of the company to AI): the highest annual recurring revenue (recurring revenue annualized, $ millions) reported for a company run by one person, as stated by the company, its founder, its investors or a payment-provider-verified dashboard (the note grades the verification; total revenue not stated as recurring does not count); obs = the date the figure refers to; a row only when the record grows. One person (owner 2026-10-28): no employees, and nobody else builds the product or runs operations, whether contractors, an agency or another company's staff; incidental professional services (legal, accounting) and ordinary vendors' products are fine. A row needs a source stating the one-person setup and no source contradicting it for that time: Polsia from mid-2026 does not count (its founder said on 2026-10-16 that engineers of Sapiom were pulled into the product to fix bugs and harden the platform). Founder hours are not required here: the oversight clause is the AI side's series, unattended-business-arr-max

Directly measured AI software task horizon at 80% success (human expert hours), measured on SWE-Marathon v1.1 (Abundant AI; 20 software tasks with expert time estimates of 4-400 h, binary rewards, about 8 trials per task and configuration): per agent/model/effort configuration, METR's logistic fit P(success) = 1/(1+exp(-beta (log2 h50 - log2 t))) by maximum likelihood over its trials (harness-error trials excluded; degenerate fits dropped); per model the configuration with the highest h80; release-cohort: the highest value among models released on or before the obs date (release date per Epoch's ECI file, else the model's first SWE-Marathon trial); current site vintage, earlier dates re-stated (gather/collectors/swe_marathon.py, robots_software.py)

Directly measured AI software task horizon at 50% success (human expert hours), measured on SWE-Marathon v1.1 (Abundant AI; 20 software tasks with expert time estimates of 4-400 h, binary rewards, about 8 trials per task and configuration): per agent/model/effort configuration, METR's logistic fit P(success) = 1/(1+exp(-beta (log2 h50 - log2 t))) by maximum likelihood over its trials (harness-error trials excluded; degenerate fits dropped); per model the configuration with the highest h80; release-cohort: the highest value among models released on or before the obs date (release date per Epoch's ECI file, else the model's first SWE-Marathon trial); current site vintage, earlier dates re-stated (gather/collectors/swe_marathon.py, robots_software.py)

Cross-check of the frozen ECI -> METR calibration (not a KPI input; read by the task-horizon driver's tripwire, drivers.yaml): per month (obs YYYY-MM, as of the month end or the retrieval date), the mean over SWE-Marathon's frontier models of log2(measured 80% horizon, swe-marathon-h80-by-release's best configuration by h80) - log2(the 80% horizon horizon-80-software-eci's calibration gives the same model's ECI), in doublings; frontier models = models with an ECI score released by then within 5 ECI points of the ECI frontier then; no such model = no row (gather/collectors/robots_software.py)

Cross-check of the frozen ECI -> METR calibration (not a KPI input; read by the task-horizon driver's tripwire, drivers.yaml): per month (obs YYYY-MM, as of the month end or the retrieval date), the mean over METR Time Horizon 1.1's frontier models of log2(METR's 80% horizon) - log2(the 80% horizon horizon-80-software-eci's calibration gives the same model's ECI), in doublings; models mapped to ECI names in the collector's CALIBRATION_PAIRS (the calibration's own models are in-sample residuals; a new METR model is the out-of-sample check); frontier models = released by then within 5 ECI points of the ECI frontier then; no such model = no row (gather/collectors/robots_software.py)

Release-cohort Terminal-Bench 4.0 resolution rate (tbench.ai / Harbor Hub leaderboard 4-0-0; 66 agentic terminal tasks with expert time estimates of 0.75-60 h, median 4 h, 5 trials each): the highest share of resolved trials among leaderboard configurations (any agent and reasoning effort) of models released on or before the obs date (the leaderboard's release date); not converted to hours (its time estimates do not predict failures); a cross-check of the robots-software horizon pace, independent of ECI (gather/collectors/terminal_bench.py, robots_software.py)

Release-cohort frontier of UK AISI's 80%-reliability cyber time horizon (human hours) on its narrow CTF task suite with a 2.5M-token budget per task (reasoning models only): the best among models AISI evaluated that were RELEASED by the obs date, read off the figure of AISI's post (no data file is published; ledger/audits/2026-10-18-aisi-cyber digitize.py); a pace and ECI-slope cross-check of the KPI, its level is cyber- and budget-specific and not METR-comparable

Precursor of the-10m-solopreneur, the AI side (businesses an AI already runs on little human time, growing in revenue): the highest annualized revenue ($ millions) of a real business (paying customers outside its operators; not a simulation or benchmark) whose operating decisions an AI system makes (what to sell, prices, purchasing, marketing, customer handling), whose total human time running it is stated by a source to be under 10 hours a week over the period, and which did not lose money over it (owner 2026-10-28). Human time = the owner plus everyone working for it, including staff, gig workers or restockers doing tasks the AI directs; incidental professional services (legal, accounting) excluded. Not losing money = revenue at least all costs over the period, including AI compute/tokens and paid human work. Annualized revenue = sales over a stated period of at least one month x 12 / months (pass-through and one-off asset sales excluded; unlike the milestone, the revenue need not be recurring). obs = the period's end; a row only when the record grows; the note gives the period, the hours and profit statements and who makes them, and grades the verification (operator-stated, third-party, payment-provider-verified)

Precursor of the-linux-kernel-patch, the AI side (AI agents submitting code themselves): the largest single code contribution (pull request, patch or patch series) that an AI agent submitted and took through review, merged into a major open-source project (OS kernel, compiler, language runtime, browser engine, core library, or a comparably maintained project), in lines added per the merge record; obs = merge date; a row only when the record grows (owner 2026-10-28). AI-submitted: the agent opened it (an agent or bot account, or the project or the person who tasked the agent says the agent submitted it); its code commits are the agent's (humans may assign the task, review and comment; human-authored commits beyond trivial fixups disqualify); where review asked for changes, the agent made them. Independent acceptance: approved by a maintainer other than the person who assigned or directed the agent, in a project that neither that person nor the agent's or model's developer controls (owns it, or leads it alone). The note names the project, the agent and AI system, who tasked it and who approved it
